confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Varanasi prices. Beer, coffee and inexpensive and mid-range meals come from crowdsourced cost-of-living sites (MyLifeElsewhere, Numbeo-style mirrors, CityCost, Expatistan). Those sites disagree with each other, so I took rounded central values. Beer is set above the roughly ₹150 listed because restaurant and bar menus usually charge more. Cocktail and wine are the weakest anchors. I found only one thin cocktail estimate (about AU$4.85 in a downtown club, per Expatistan) and no Varanasi wine-by-the-glass price. I set both from the local beer price and typical hotel-bar pricing in India. Alcohol is sold in only a limited number of venues in Varanasi, mainly hotel bars. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Varanasi's hostel and hotel market and of Indian pricing. I did not search for or inspect any accommodation listings or booking pages. The RBA observation was taken from the RBA exchange-rates page as reported in search results, not read directly from the page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Varanasi's own crowdsourced food and drink price data. Accommodation is benchmarked against other mid-sized Indian pilgrimage and backpacker cities such as Rishikesh, Pushkar and Agra, with a modest premium for the ghat-area guesthouse and hostel market.
